samples: This program reads the fixed file `data/server.log`, parses each non-blank line as a timestamp, a severity level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR) and a message, and prints how many ERROR entries occurred in each date-and-hour bucket, earliest first. Hours with no errors are not listed. Before relying on it, note that the path is hardcoded and that one malformed line, an unrecognised level such as TRACE, or a line with no message text makes the whole run fail with an error and print nothing. It is therefore best suited to clean, uniformly formatted logs, and the only ready-made pieces to reuse are the line parser and the per-hour counter.

This program reads a fixed file, `data/server.log`, treats each non-blank line as a timestamp, a severity level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR) and a message, and prints how many ERROR entries occurred in each hour, earliest first, in the form "date-and-hour: N errors". It is all-or-nothing: a single malformed line, a bad timestamp or an unrecognized level such as TRACE stops the whole run with an error and no report. Hours with no errors are not listed, the file path is hardcoded rather than passed in, and the program only reads that file and writes to the console.

This program reads the fixed file `data/server.log`, parses each non-blank line as a timestamp, a severity level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR) and a message, and prints how many ERROR entries occurred in each hour, earliest hour first. It is strict: a single malformed line or unknown level stops the whole run with an error rather than being skipped, and hours with no errors are not listed. The path is hard-coded, so you can't point it at another file without editing it, and the step that groups errors by hour doesn't end with a result clause like the grouping examples in the cheat sheet, so it may not pass the checker as written.

This program reads the fixed file `data/server.log`, where each non-blank line is a timestamp, a level (DEBUG, INFO, WARN or ERROR) and a message. It counts the ERROR lines per date-and-hour and prints one line per hour, earliest first, so hours with no errors don't appear. It is strict: a single malformed line or unknown level aborts the whole run with an error instead of being skipped, and the path can't be changed without editing the program. The grouping step in the error-counting function has no closing clause such as `collect` or `sum`, unlike the group-by forms in the cheat sheet, so check that it compiles before relying on it.

This program reads the fixed file `data/server.log`, parses each non-blank line as a timestamp, a severity level and a message, and prints how many error-level entries occurred in each hour, earliest hour first (hours with no errors are not listed). It is strict: a single malformed line or unrecognized level, or an unreadable file, aborts the whole run with an error rather than skipping the line. The file path is hard-coded and only `WARN` (not `WARNING`) is accepted as the warning level, so you would need to adapt it for other logs, and the hour-grouping step is written in a form the cheat sheet doesn't show, so it should be checked before you rely on it.
